DomainsPage.title: Domains
DomainsPage.subtitle: Reach your containers with your own domain names and HTTPS.
DomainsPage.loadFailed: Could not load the domain settings of this environment.
DomainsPage.blockedTitle: A proxy is already in the way
DomainsPage.blockedExisting: This environment already runs a reverse proxy (Traefik or Caddy) that Shipir does not manage. To avoid two proxies fighting over the same ports, Shipir does not set up another one here.
DomainsPage.blockedPorts: Port 80 or 443 is already used by a container on this environment. A reverse proxy needs both ports, so stop or move that container first.
DomainsPage.adminOnly: Only administrators can set up the reverse proxy. Ask an administrator to set it up, then you can publish containers here.
DomainsPage.readyText: The reverse proxy is managed by Shipir and routes your domains to your containers.
DomainsPage.noDomainsHint: Published domains will be listed here.
DomainsPage.setupFailed: The setup did not finish. Check the output above and the proxy deployment for details.
ProxySetupCard.title: Set up the reverse proxy
ProxySetupCard.intro: A reverse proxy listens on ports 80 and 443 and sends each domain to the right container. Shipir runs it for you.
ProxySetupCard.traefikDesc: Popular and flexible. Supports wildcard certificates.
ProxySetupCard.caddyDesc: Simple and lightweight. Certificates just work.
ProxySetupCard.emailHelpRequired: Let’s Encrypt sends expiry warnings here.
ProxySetupCard.emailHelpOptional: Optional. Let’s Encrypt sends expiry warnings here.
ProxySetupCard.emailRequired: Enter an e-mail address for Let’s Encrypt.
ProxySetupCard.automaticDesc: Free certificates, requested and renewed for you.
ProxySetupCard.ownDesc: Use a certificate you bought or created yourself.
ProxySetupCard.ownNote: The proxy starts with automatic Let’s Encrypt certificates as its default. Once it runs, upload your own certificate under Your certificates and assign it to a domain.
errors.forbidden: You are not allowed to set up the reverse proxy here.
errors.proxyExists: This environment already has a proxy managed by Shipir.
errors.setupBlocked: Another proxy is already running, or port 80 or 443 is in use on this environment. Free the ports and try again.
errors.unsupported: This option is not supported by the chosen proxy. Pick Traefik or change the setting.
errors.invalidEmail: This e-mail address does not look valid.
errors.noEncryptionKey: The server has no encryption key configured, so the setup cannot store its settings.
CertificatesSection.title: Your certificates
CertificatesSection.intro: Certificates you uploaded yourself. Assign one to a domain when you publish a container.
CertificatesSection.name: Name
CertificatesSection.loadFailed: Could not load the certificates of this environment.
CertificatesSection.emptyAdmin: Upload a certificate you bought or created yourself, together with its private key. Shipir stores the key encrypted and never shows it again.
CertificatesSection.emptyReadOnly: There are no certificates to show. Only administrators can upload certificates, so ask an administrator if you need one for a domain.
CertificatesSection.deleteText: The certificate and its key are removed from the proxy. This cannot be undone.
CertificateDialog.uploadIntro: Paste the certificate chain and the private key, or pick the files.
CertificateDialog.renewIntro: Upload the new certificate chain and its private key. Domains using this certificate switch over right away.
CertificateDialog.name: Name
CertificateDialog.nameHelp: Only for you, to tell certificates apart.
CertificateDialog.nameRequired: Enter a name for the certificate.
CertificateDialog.chainHelp: PEM format, your certificate first, then the intermediate certificates.
CertificateDialog.keyHelp: PEM format, without a password. It is never shown again after you send it.
certErrors.invalidName: The name must be 1 to 100 characters long.
certErrors.nameTaken: This name is already used by another certificate.
certErrors.invalidCertificate: This does not look like a valid PEM certificate chain.
certErrors.notYetValid: This certificate is not valid yet.
certErrors.doesNotCover: The new certificate does not cover every domain that currently uses this one.
certErrors.invalidKey: This does not look like a valid PEM private key.
certErrors.keyEncrypted: This key is protected by a password. Remove the password first, then upload it again.
certErrors.keyMismatch: This key does not belong to this certificate. Check that you picked the matching key.
certErrors.tooLarge: The certificate or key is too large.
certErrors.inUse: This certificate is still used by {{routes}}. Switch those domains to another certificate first.
certErrors.notFound: This certificate no longer exists. Reload the page.
CertificateDialog.fileTooLarge: This file is too large (the limit is {{size}} KB). Check that you picked the right file.
CertificateDialog.fileUnreadable: Could not read this file. Try again or paste the contents.
